title: Choose codeloom's visual world
question: The roll assigned Gallery Guide. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Sketches show the Home screen.

options.label: Gallery Guide
options.lineage: museum exhibitions: painted gallery walls, wall labels, audio-guide stop numbers
options.thesis: Learn a codebase like walking a museum: each user journey is an exhibit with numbered stops.
options.viewport: Viridian rail on the left; Home shows the workspace counts in a tight ruled strip, then the journey list as wall labels, each with its numbered stop roundels.
options.risk: If the roundels are timid it collapses into a generic green dashboard.

raised.raise: Every journey carries the same fixed nameplate: name, area, owner, one-line note, spec state.
Home counts sit in a strict hairline module grid with no padded hero tiles.
Seen → toured → understood is one fixed-scale strip on a shared baseline in every row.
Table columns never move; only their values change.

options.label: Line Diagram
options.lineage: metro line diagrams on midnight enamel
options.thesis: Every user journey is a coloured line; files are stations; FE/BE/DB are fare zones.
options.viewport: Navy rail; Home lists journeys as line badges, the selected one drawn as a straight line strip through UI → API → DB stations.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on product clarity (a journey literally is a line); this was also my own top-ranked idea.
options.risk: Transit maps are a familiar dev-tool metaphor; dense workspaces need many line colours.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport gate boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: When code under a journey you understood changes, its row lights up and stays lit until you re-walk it.
options.viewport: Home is a board ranked by what needs you: changed journeys lit in orange on top, then unexplored, then understood.
options.case: Holds product clarity: honest progress needs 'understanding goes stale'; weaker on the fun of learning.
options.risk: Feels like an ops monitor rather than a place to learn.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: Journeys as a ranked roster of characters.
options.viewport: A roster grid of journey mascots.
options.case: Developers don't see their code as mascots; hides files and SQL.
options.kept: Fixed nameplate furniture on every journey.

options.label: High-Density Grid
options.thesis: Pack every number on one screen.
options.case: Too dense for long learning sessions.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Understanding grows in stages like a plant.
options.case: Poetic but weak fit for code structure.
options.kept: Progress stages at fixed scale on a shared baseline.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.viewport: A black flap board of journeys.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dev-tool dashboard like Linear or Sourcegraph, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Dark sidebar, stat cards, a sortable journey table.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other dev tool by design.
